summary.text: A 22-year-old man with a road traffic accident four years earlier, a left frontal bone fracture and left frontal encephalocele, and a previous severe pneumococcal meningitis last year presented to the emergency department with fever and cough of one week and headache, irritability and vomiting of one day. Examination showed a temperature of 37.6 °C and positive nuchal rigidity without focal deficits.

Initial CT showed hydrocephalus and left frontal lobe findings suggestive of an inflammatory or abscess collection, and papilledema was excluded by fundoscopy before lumbar puncture. Serum and CSF results fitted a bacterial meningitis pattern and blood and CSF cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae. MRI with contrast confirmed meningitis and showed a collection highly suggestive of an abscess of about 2 x 1 cm.

He received empiric IV ceftriaxone, vancomycin and dexamethasone, then targeted IV ceftriaxone. He was offered surgery for the abscess but opted for medical management. Fever resolved, WBC count normalized, headache lessened, and repeat MRI showed a smaller abscess without need for intensive care.

The infectious disease team recommended six weeks of IV ceftriaxone and pneumococcal and meningococcal vaccines, and specialists recommended surgery for the osseous defects, which the patient refused. Repeat blood culture after the antibiotic course was negative. At neurosurgery follow-up he was asymptomatic and free of any recurrence for seven months after discharge.
